**Short answer:** The delivery problem is real in what customers say, and it accounts for WA's NPS fall. I can't confirm it from operations data, though, because Baby Mart holds no home-delivery or click-and-collect records.

## What changed
- **It started in early March.** Delivery complaints have been running high since the week of 2 March 2026, so I measured from there rather than from late April.
- **NPS dropped hard.** WA NPS fell from 31.6 to 4.5 (−27.1 pts) on 266 responses. The detractor rate rose from 23.1% to 39.5%.
- **WA fell faster than the country.** National NPS fell −16.5 pts over the same window.
- **The last three weeks look flat for a reason.** Against a baseline that already includes March, NPS moved only +1.3 pts, because complaints were already high in that baseline.
- **The week of 4 May is partial**, so its NPS of 43.8 shouldn't be read as a recovery.



## Where
- **Three Perth stores explain 66.1% of the fall:**
  - Midland: −63.5 pts
  - Perth CBD: −43.3 pts
  - Karrinyup: −29.6 pts
- **Not limited to a product range:** every category fell.
- **Not limited to a member tier:** Silver & Bronze members are 73.3% of responses, so their fall is simply WA's fall.

## What customers said
Delivery and click-and-collect complaints rose from 0.5 a week to 7.8 a week (15.7x), 75 in total, 44 of them from detractors.
- "My click and collect order at Karrinyup was three days late."
- The same complaint also came in through an NPS survey.
- Other survey comments: "Home delivery to Perth took nearly two weeks." and "Click and collect was ready but nobody could find my order."

## What we tested
| Hypothesis | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Store | Top 3 stores explain 66.1% of the fall | CONFIRMED |
| Category | Every category fell (Nappies & Wipes −34.3 pts, rest −24.4 pts) | RULED_OUT |
| Tier | Silver & Bronze is 73.3% of responses, so it is WA as a whole | RULED_OUT |
| Theme | Delivery complaints up 15.7x | CONFIRMED |
| **Delivery ops** | Inbound to the WA DC was 82.5% on time and 97.6% filled, but there are only 5 earlier order lines to compare against, and no last-mile or click-and-collect data | **INCONCLUSIVE** |
| Stock | Out-of-stock mentions only 1.7x usual; 20% name Uppababy | RULED_OUT |
| Campaign | Top campaign drew 1.3% of negative comments | RULED_OUT |
| Supply | Uppababy supplier on-time-in-full rate up from 90.3% to 91.9% | RULED_OUT |
| Price | Complaints 1.5x; competitor price gap steady (5.9% → 5.7%) | RULED_OUT |
| App | 5 complaints | RULED_OUT |
| Quality | Bugaboo 1.1 a week vs 0.8 | RULED_OUT |

## What to do
1. **Digital:** get the WA carrier and click-and-collect order logs from 2 March. That's the only way to confirm or rule out a real operational failure.
2. **Store Ops:** audit how click-and-collect orders are staged and found at Midland, Perth CBD and Karrinyup.
3. **Supply:** compare the WA DC's 82.5% inbound on-time rate with how quickly online orders go out to stores.
4. **CRM:** contact the 44 detractors who complained about delivery to try to win them back.
